---
title: Directive extension test
author: Dongyu Zhao
version: 0.1
date: '2026-06-22'
license: '[CC-BY-SA 4.0](http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/)'
...

## Directives

Text directives use one colon. The label parses inline Markdown. Attributes
use the generic directive attribute-list syntax inside braces. The parser
normalizes the list to a string-to-string JSON object for the AST/API without
projecting it onto the generated HTML wrapper.

Bare, unquoted, single-quoted, and double-quoted values all become strings.
The empty object is valid.

```````````````````````````````` example
Use :cite[Smith *et al.*]{id=smith class=paper data-kind=ref} here.
.
Document scope=1:1..1:67 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:67 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:4 literal="Use " children=0
    ├── Directive scope=1:5..1:61 name="cite" attributes=[class="paper" data-kind="ref" id="smith"] children=1
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:10..1:25 children=2
    │       ├── Text scope=1:11..1:16 literal="Smith " children=0
    │       └── Emphasis scope=1:17..1:24 children=1
    │           └── Text scope=1:18..1:23 literal="et al." children=0
    └── Text scope=1:62..1:67 literal=" here." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Inline attribute lists may span source lines. Their full source range belongs
to the directive, and subsequent inline nodes resume at the physical line and
column after the closing brace.

```````````````````````````````` example
:note[label]{title="one
two"} tail
.
Document scope=1:1..2:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..2:5 name="note" attributes=[title="one\ntwo"] children=1
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:12 children=1
    │       └── Text scope=1:7..1:11 literal="label" children=0
    └── Text scope=2:6..2:10 literal=" tail" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Numeric- and boolean-looking values remain strings in the normalized AST/API
JSON representation.

```````````````````````````````` example
:video{id=123 muted=true title="My Video"}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:42 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:42 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:42 name="video" attributes=[id="123" muted="true" title="My Video"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

An explicit empty attributes object is valid and is distinct from no
attributes object in the AST/API.

```````````````````````````````` example
:empty{}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:8 name="empty" attributes=[] children=0
````````````````````````````````

Attribute values are normalized to strings. Bare attributes become empty
strings, the last duplicate key wins, and quoted values may contain spaces.

```````````````````````````````` example
:data[label]{muted dup=first dup=last unicode=中文😀 title="My Video"}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:74 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:74 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:74 name="data" attributes=[dup="last" muted="" title="My Video" unicode="中文😀"] children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:12 children=1
            └── Text scope=1:7..1:11 literal="label" children=0
````````````````````````````````

`id` and `class` are ordinary keys. Like every repeated key, their last value
wins while their first source position is retained.

```````````````````````````````` example
:ordinary[label]{id=first class=red class=green class=blue id=last key=value}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:77 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:77 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:77 name="ordinary" attributes=[class="red green blue" id="last" key="value"] children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:10..1:16 children=1
            └── Text scope=1:11..1:15 literal="label" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Malformed and unclosed attribute lists are not consumed as directive
attributes and remain ordinary Markdown text.

```````````````````````````````` example
:invalid{=value}
:open{title="value}
.
Document scope=1:1..2:19 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:19 children=5
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:8 name="invalid" attributes=null children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:9..1:16 literal="{=value}" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:17..1:17 children=0
    ├── Directive scope=2:1..2:5 name="open" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=2:6..2:19 literal="{title=\"value}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

HTML-style `#id` and `.class` shortcuts are outside this extension's generic
key-value grammar and remain ordinary Markdown text.

```````````````````````````````` example
:shortcut{#identifier}
:shortcut{.class}
.
Document scope=1:1..2:17 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:17 children=3
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:22 name="shortcut" attributes=[id="identifier"] children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:23..1:23 children=0
    └── Directive scope=2:1..2:17 name="shortcut" attributes=[class="class"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

Text directive labels can contain links.

```````````````````````````````` example
:note[See [docs](https://example.com).]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:39 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:39 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:39 name="note" attributes=null children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:39 children=3
            ├── Text scope=1:7..1:10 literal="See " children=0
            ├── Link scope=1:11..1:37 destination="https://example.com" title=null children=1
            │   └── Text scope=1:12..1:15 literal="docs" children=0
            └── Text scope=1:38..1:38 literal="." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Text directive labels can contain bracketed text that is not a link.

```````````````````````````````` example
:note[See [plain] text.]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:24 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:24 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:24 name="note" attributes=null children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:24 children=1
            └── Text scope=1:7..1:23 literal="See [plain] text." children=0
````````````````````````````````

Text directives can appear inside link text.

```````````````````````````````` example
[Go :badge[beta]](/roadmap)
.
Document scope=1:1..1:27 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:27 children=1
    └── Link scope=1:1..1:27 destination="/roadmap" title=null children=2
        ├── Text scope=1:2..1:4 literal="Go " children=0
        └── Directive scope=1:5..1:16 name="badge" attributes=null children=1
            └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:11..1:16 children=1
                └── Text scope=1:12..1:15 literal="beta" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Text directives can appear inside table cells.

```````````````````````````````` example table
| status |
| --- |
| :badge[beta] |
.
Document scope=1:1..3:16 children=1
└── Table scope=1:1..3:16 alignments=[none] children=2
    ├── TableRow scope=1:1..1:10 isHeader=true children=1
    │   └── TableCell scope=1:2..1:9 children=1
    │       └── Text scope=1:3..1:8 literal="status" children=0
    └── TableRow scope=3:1..3:16 isHeader=false children=1
        └── TableCell scope=3:2..3:15 children=1
            └── Directive scope=3:3..3:14 name="badge" attributes=null children=1
                └── DirectiveLabel scope=3:9..3:14 children=1
                    └── Text scope=3:10..3:13 literal="beta" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A text directive with only a name is not recognized when it is followed by a
colon, so gemoji-compatible text remains text.

```````````````````````````````` example
:red:
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal=":red:" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An empty label disambiguates a text directive before a following colon.

```````````````````````````````` example
:red[]:
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:6 name="red" attributes=null children=1
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:5..1:6 children=0
    └── Text scope=1:7..1:7 literal=":" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A LABEL IS SCANNED AT THE COLON, not paired with a closer found later. Both
branches continue, exactly as the attribute block's do: a label that closes is a
label, a label that does not is prose, and the directive stands either way.

```````````````````````````````` example
:a[b and :c[
.
Document scope=1:1..1:12 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:12 children=4
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="a" attributes=null children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:3..1:9 literal="[b and " children=0
    ├── Directive scope=1:10..1:11 name="c" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:12..1:12 literal="[" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Because the whole construct is consumed there, nothing else is ever offered its
bytes. An emphasis run opened before the directive cannot pair with a marker
inside the label, and a code span inside one cannot protect the `]` that ends
it -- the label ended before either was looked for.

```````````````````````````````` example
*a :b[c*]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:3 literal="*a " children=0
    └── Directive scope=1:4..1:9 name="b" attributes=null children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:6..1:9 children=1
            └── Text scope=1:7..1:8 literal="c*" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:b[a`b]`c]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:7 name="b" attributes=null children=1
    │   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:3..1:7 children=1
    │       └── Text scope=1:4..1:6 literal="a`b" children=0
    └── Text scope=1:8..1:10 literal="`c]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The scan is lexical: only a backslash escape and bracket balance decide where
the label ends, and nesting is capped at 32 as micromark caps it. Thirty-two
nested brackets are a label and thirty-three are prose.

```````````````````````````````` example
:a[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[x]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:69 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:69 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:69 name="a" attributes=null children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:3..1:69 children=1
            └── Text scope=1:4..1:68 literal="[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[x]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:a[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[x]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:71 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:71 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="a" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:71 literal="[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[[x]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A directive name may contain a hyphen or underscore but may not begin or end
with one. This example previously expected `:-a[]` and `:_a[]` to be
directives; scripts/check-mdast-parity.mjs found the disagreement with
micromark-extension-directive, which rejects both. Its prose documents only the
trailing rule, so the leading one was confirmed against the implementation
directly: `:-a[]` and `:_a[]` produce no directive there, while `:1a[]` does.

```````````````````````````````` example
:a-[]
:-a[]
:_a[]
.
Document scope=1:1..3:5 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..3:5 children=5
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal=":a-[]" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:6..1:6 children=0
    ├── Text scope=2:1..2:5 literal=":-a[]" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=2:6..2:6 children=0
    └── Text scope=3:1..3:5 literal=":_a[]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A digit may begin a name, as it may in the reference implementation.

```````````````````````````````` example
:1a[]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:5 name="1a" attributes=null children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:4..1:5 children=0
````````````````````````````````

A name is CODE POINTS, like every other name in this grammar. `:café` is one
directive, not a directive called `caf` followed by the letter `é`, and the
block forms read the same names the inline form does.

```````````````````````````````` example
:café[x]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 name="café" attributes=null children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:7..1:9 children=1
            └── Text scope=1:8..1:8 literal="x" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
::naïve{a=1}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:13 children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..1:13 name="naïve" attributes=[a="1"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

And punctuation ends a name whatever its width, which is the half a byte-wise
scan gets wrong in the other direction: an en dash is one code point of
punctuation and three bytes of none.

```````````````````````````````` example
a :b–c d
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=3
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:2 literal="a " children=0
    ├── Directive scope=1:3..1:4 name="b" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:5..1:10 literal="–c d" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An unquoted value may hold no quote of either kind, alongside the four it may
hold no `<`, `>`, `=` or backtick. Reaching one does not end the value, it
makes the block malformed.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a=b"c"}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="n" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:10 literal="{a=b\"c\"}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An underscore may not end a name either, the same as a hyphen.

```````````````````````````````` example
:a_[]
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal=":a_[]" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Leaf directives use two colons on their own line. Repeated metadata keys use
their last value and are not projected onto HTML.

```````````````````````````````` example
::youtube[Video of a *cat*]{vid=01ab2cd3efg class=embed class=featured}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:71 children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..1:71 name="youtube" attributes=[class="embed featured" vid="01ab2cd3efg"] children=1
    └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:10..1:27 children=2
        ├── Text scope=1:11..1:21 literal="Video of a " children=0
        └── Emphasis scope=1:22..1:26 children=1
            └── Text scope=1:23..1:25 literal="cat" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Container directives use three or more colons on their own line. A closing
fence must have at least the opening fence length.

```````````````````````````````` example
::::spoiler{id=outer class=red class=green class=blue}
He dies.

:::spoiler
She is born.
:::
::::
.
Document scope=1:1..7:4 children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..7:4 name="spoiler" attributes=[class="red green blue" id="outer"] children=2
    ├── Paragraph scope=2:1..2:8 children=1
    │   └── Text scope=2:1..2:8 literal="He dies." children=0
    └── DirectiveBlock scope=4:1..6:3 name="spoiler" attributes=null children=1
        └── Paragraph scope=5:1..5:12 children=1
            └── Text scope=5:1..5:12 literal="She is born." children=0
````````````````````````````````

If no closing fence is found, the container runs to the end of its parent.

```````````````````````````````` example
::::spoiler
These three are not enough to close
:::
So this line is also part of the container.
.
Document scope=1:1..4:43 children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..4:43 name="spoiler" attributes=null children=1
    └── Paragraph scope=2:1..4:43 children=5
        ├── Text scope=2:1..2:35 literal="These three are not enough to close" children=0
        ├── SoftBreak scope=2:36..2:36 children=0
        ├── Text scope=3:1..3:3 literal=":::" children=0
        ├── SoftBreak scope=3:4..3:4 children=0
        └── Text scope=4:1..4:43 literal="So this line is also part of the container." children=0
````````````````````````````````

An indented colon run inside a container is content, not a closing fence.

```````````````````````````````` example
:::spoiler
    :::
:::
.
Document scope=1:1..3:3 children=1
└── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..3:3 name="spoiler" attributes=null children=1
    └── CodeBlock scope=2:5..2:7 info=null language=null literal=":::\n" fenced=false closed=true children=0
````````````````````````````````

The directive trigger characters are ordinary punctuation for emphasis
flanking: an underscore after `:` or `}` still opens emphasis exactly as
reference CommonMark requires.

```````````````````````````````` example
foo:_bar_
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:4 literal="foo:" children=0
    └── Emphasis scope=1:5..1:9 children=1
        └── Text scope=1:6..1:8 literal="bar" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
a}_b_
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:2 literal="a}" children=0
    └── Emphasis scope=1:3..1:5 children=1
        └── Text scope=1:4..1:4 literal="b" children=0
````````````````````````````````

`#name` and `.name` are shorthand for the `id` and `class` attributes. A
shorthand value ends at the next marker, so `{.a.b}` is two classes rather
than one class named `a.b`.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a.b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:8 name="n" attributes=[class="a b"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

`class` is the one attribute whose repeats accumulate, in source order, whether
they were written as shorthand or as `class=`. Every other name keeps the last
value.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{class=x .y}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:14 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:14 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:14 name="n" attributes=[class="x y"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

`id` keeps the last value, like an ordinary name.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{#a#b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:8 name="n" attributes=[id="b"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

A shorthand marker with no name after it is not a valid attribute and
invalidates the block, which then takes the malformed-block fallback: the name
stands and the braces stay as text.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{#}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="n" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:5 literal="{#}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="n" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:5 literal="{.}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An ordinary attribute whose name is as long as `class` is not treated as one.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{other=1 .a .b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:17 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:17 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:17 name="n" attributes=[class="a b" other="1"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

The separator goes before every class value once something has accumulated, an
empty value included.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a class="" .b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:18 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:18 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:18 name="n" attributes=[class="a  b"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

An empty value at the front accumulates nothing, so it contributes no leading
separator.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{class="" .b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:15 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:15 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:15 name="n" attributes=[class="b"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

Shorthand also reaches the label-close probe, which validates the attribute
block after `]` before the label is accepted.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n[label]{#i .c}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:16 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:16 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:16 name="n" attributes=[class="c" id="i"] children=1
        └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:3..1:9 children=1
            └── Text scope=1:4..1:8 literal="label" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A text directive's colon may not sit next to another colon on either side. The
trailing rule keeps `:red:` available to emoji; the leading one keeps a run of
colons whole, so a run inside a paragraph is text rather than a shorter run
plus a directive. `::name` and `:::name` at the start of a line are leaf and
container directives and open through the block path instead.

```````````````````````````````` example
x ::a y
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:7 literal="x ::a y" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A longer run behaves the same way; the directive never starts inside it.

```````````````````````````````` example
x ::::a y
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:9 literal="x ::::a y" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A colon run with no space before it is text as well.

```````````````````````````````` example
x:::a
.
Document scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:5 children=1
    └── Text scope=1:1..1:5 literal="x:::a" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A quoted value must be separated from whatever follows it by whitespace or the
closing brace. Without that rule an unterminated quote lets the block run on
and swallow the rest of the paragraph.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a="x"b=1}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:12 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:12 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="n" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:12 literal="{a=\"x\"b=1}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An attribute name may not begin with punctuation, so a leading colon makes
the whole block invalid and it falls back to text. `:` and `.` are allowed
from the second character on, which is why `{a:b}` is a name.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{:_a}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:7 literal="{:_a}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A symbol is punctuation for this rule too.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a$b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:7 literal="{a$b}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Letters outside ASCII are names, not punctuation; the grammar is applied to
code points rather than bytes.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{中文=1}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:12 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:12 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:12 name="x" attributes=[中文="1"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

`:` and `.` inside a name are ordinary name characters.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a:b .c}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:10 name="x" attributes=[a:b="" class="c"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

A name may begin with a hyphen or an underscore, unlike a DIRECTIVE name, which
may not. Every other punctuation mark still ends the block.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{-a=1 _b=2}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:13 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:13 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:13 name="n" attributes=[-a="1" _b="2"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

A shorthand value is not a name. It ends at the next marker, at the block's end
or at whitespace, and six characters -- a quote of either kind, `<`, `=`, `>`
and a backtick -- reject it outright and take the block with them. Everything
else is a value character, so a class may contain an ampersand.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a&b .c$d}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:13 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:13 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:13 name="n" attributes=[class="a&b c$d"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a=b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="n" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:8 literal="{.a=b}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The two quotes are the same rule, but they never reach it: the raw scan of the
block tracks quoting, so `{.a"b}` has no closing brace outside a quote and is
malformed one step earlier. `=`, `<`, `>` and the backtick are the four that
this rule alone decides -- a pin on a quote proves nothing here, which a mutant
that deleted the whole reject set and survived is what said so.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{.a`b}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="n" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:8 literal="{.a`b}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

Character references are decoded in an attribute's value, and in a shorthand's
value, and nowhere else in the attribute block: a name is taken as written
(Q20). An unknown reference is not a reference and stays as written.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a=&amp; b="&amp; &#65; &#x41;" .&amp; c=&notreal;}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:53 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:53 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:53 name="n" attributes=[a="&" b="& A A" c="&notreal;" class="&"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

The decoding happens after the block has been scanned, never during it, so a
reference cannot produce a character that changes where the block ends or where
one attribute stops and the next begins.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a=x&#125;y b=p&#32;q}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:24 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:24 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:24 name="n" attributes=[a="x}y" b="p q"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

A reference in a NAME is not decoded, so `&` is what the name starts with, and
that is punctuation: the block is malformed and its source stays text -- where
the ordinary inline rules do decode it.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{&#97;=v}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:11 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:11 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="n" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:11 literal="{a=v}" children=0
````````````````````````````````

**This engine requires the semicolon**, as CommonMark does and as it does at
every other place a reference is decoded -- a link destination, a link title, a
fenced block's info string. micromark-extension-directive does not, in this one
construct and nowhere else in its own parser; the difference is registered in
specs/mdast-parity/deltas.json and measured there.

```````````````````````````````` example
:n{a=&amp b=&#65}
.
Document scope=1:1..1:17 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:17 children=1
    └── Directive scope=1:1..1:17 name="n" attributes=[a="&amp" b="&#65"] children=0
````````````````````````````````

A leaf directive is a single line: the next line starts new content rather than
continuing it, unlike a container, which runs until its fence.

```````````````````````````````` example
::leaf[L]{a=b}
after
.
Document scope=1:1..2:5 children=2
├── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..1:14 name="leaf" attributes=[a="b"] children=1
│   └── DirectiveLabel scope=1:7..1:9 children=1
│       └── Text scope=1:8..1:8 literal="L" children=0
└── Paragraph scope=2:1..2:5 children=1
    └── Text scope=2:1..2:5 literal="after" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An `=` promises a value. With none before the block ends, the whole attribute
block is malformed and its source stays text — an empty value would otherwise be
indistinguishable from the valueless `{a}`, which means something else.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:7 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:7 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:7 literal="{a=}t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The same when only whitespace separates the `=` from the closer, and when the
block spans a line ending.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a= }t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:8 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:8 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:8 literal="{a= }t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=
}t
.
Document scope=1:1..2:2 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:2 children=4
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    ├── Text scope=1:3..1:5 literal="{a=" children=0
    ├── SoftBreak scope=1:6..1:6 children=0
    └── Text scope=2:1..2:2 literal="}t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An unquoted value may not contain `<`, `>`, `=`, or a backtick. Reaching one
does not end the value, it makes the block malformed.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b<c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:10 literal="{a=b<c}t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b>c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:10 literal="{a=b>c}t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b=c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:10 literal="{a=b=c}t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b`c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:2 name="x" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:3..1:10 literal="{a=b`c}t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A brace is not in that set: it is an ordinary character inside an unquoted
value, and a space ends the value and starts the next attribute's name.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b{c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 name="x" attributes=[a="b{c"] children=0
    └── Text scope=1:10..1:10 literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=b c}t
.
Document scope=1:1..1:10 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:10 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:9 name="x" attributes=[a="b" c=""] children=0
    └── Text scope=1:10..1:10 literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

An unquoted value may span a line ending before it starts; the value itself is
what may not.

```````````````````````````````` example
:x{a=
b}t
.
Document scope=1:1..2:3 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..2:3 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..2:2 name="x" attributes=[a="b"] children=0
    └── Text scope=2:3..2:3 literal="t" children=0
````````````````````````````````

D21's own pins, which the oracle has not got: a closing fence closes the
container and every block still open inside it. They are kept here, at the end,
because the oracle's ordering is otherwise adopted whole.

```````````````````````````````` example
a}*.foo.*
.
Document scope=1:1..1:9 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:9 children=2
    ├── Text scope=1:1..1:2 literal="a}" children=0
    └── Emphasis scope=1:3..1:9 children=1
        └── Text scope=1:4..1:8 literal=".foo." children=0
````````````````````````````````

A closing fence closes the container and every block still open inside it, and
the container ends on the fence's own line. Consuming the fence without closing
the block leaves the next non-blank line to arrive as a lazy paragraph
continuation: it is pulled inside the container and recorded on the fence's
line rather than its own.

```````````````````````````````` example
:::note
body
:::
after
.
Document scope=1:1..4:5 children=2
├── DirectiveBlock scope=1:1..3:3 name="note" attributes=null children=1
│   └── Paragraph scope=2:1..2:4 children=1
│       └── Text scope=2:1..2:4 literal="body" children=0
└── Paragraph scope=4:1..4:5 children=1
    └── Text scope=4:1..4:5 literal="after" children=0
````````````````````````````````

The same, inside a block quote, where the misattribution moved content into the
quote as well.

```````````````````````````````` example
> :::note
> body
> :::
> after
.
Document scope=1:1..4:7 children=1
└── BlockQuote scope=1:1..4:7 children=2
    ├── DirectiveBlock scope=1:3..3:5 name="note" attributes=null children=1
    │   └── Paragraph scope=2:3..2:6 children=1
    │       └── Text scope=2:3..2:6 literal="body" children=0
    └── Paragraph scope=4:3..4:7 children=1
        └── Text scope=4:3..4:7 literal="after" children=0
````````````````````````````````

THE BLOCK FORM OF A DIRECTIVE HAS NO PARTIAL RECOVERY. The inline form keeps
the directive and gives up only the label or the attribute list; here one bad
attribute, or one byte of content after a good one, costs the whole line, and
what is left is a paragraph indistinguishable from prose. These examples pin
that AST behavior directly.

```````````````````````````````` example
::note{=value}

::note{a=b} trailing
.
Document scope=1:1..3:20 children=2
├── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:14 children=1
│   └── Text scope=1:1..1:14 literal="::note{=value}" children=0
└── Paragraph scope=3:1..3:20 children=1
    └── Text scope=3:1..3:20 literal="::note{a=b} trailing" children=0
````````````````````````````````

A DIRECTIVE NAME MAY CONTAIN UTF-8, AND AN UNCLOSED LABEL REMAINS PROSE.
The `é` is part of the directive name; the following bracket run is a separate
Text node because it never closes.

```````````````````````````````` example
:nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnéz[unclosed
.
Document scope=1:1..1:52 children=1
└── Paragraph scope=1:1..1:52 children=2
    ├── Directive scope=1:1..1:43 name="nnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnnéz" attributes=null children=0
    └── Text scope=1:44..1:52 literal="[unclosed" children=0
````````````````````````````````
